name: Al Riham Trail
area: Wadi Saham, in the Hajar Mountains about 15 to 20 km southwest of Fujairah City, Fujairah emirate. The route climbs Jebel Riham (also spelt Raham).
gradeBasis: Fujairah Adventures Centre, the emirate's official trail operator, grades Al Riham Trail 'Hard' and calls it a challenging mountain ridge trail. It is the only one of its 14 listed trails graded 'Hard'; Dhanha and Al Aqah are graded 'Extreme'. A commercial guide company, ECC Adventures, rates its guided Mount Riham ascent 'Intermediate (6/10)' and warns of steep grades from the start, loose rocks and exposure to heights.

distanceNote: Official figure from Fujairah Adventures Centre, which does not say whether 7.71 km is one way or the whole route. Two third-party sources give about 7 km for the same mountain (MissionsOffroad, November 2023; ECC Adventures, 7.0 km), and ECC calls its version a loop, so 7.71 km is most likely the whole route; that is an inference, not an operator statement.
climbNote: About 450 m, from MissionsOffroad (published 16 November 2023: 'around 7 km and 450 m elevation gain'). ECC Adventures gives 470 m for its guided loop. Fujairah Adventures Centre gives no ascent figure, so treat 450 to 470 m as third-party and approximate.
time: 2 to 3 hours (operator); a guided group on the same mountain is quoted 2.5 to 3.5 hours (ECC Adventures)

trailhead.name: Al Riham Trail pin, Wadi Saham (operator's Google Maps place)
trailhead.coordSource: Operator pin: the Google Maps short link that Fujairah Adventures Centre attaches to Al Riham Trail (maps.app.goo.gl/4nvyqrHTyqBnq5WN8) resolves to a place named 'Al Riham Trail' at 25.1108212, 56.2236185. A second start point is given by MissionsOffroad for the Jebel Raham hike: 25.112677, 56.211266, beside the Wadi Saham petroglyph rock (25.112754, 56.209106), about 1.3 km west of the operator pin. The two have not been reconciled.

routeDescription: Fujairah Adventures Centre says the trail starts in Wadi Saham, passes water springs and climbs to the top of the mountain. Wadi Saham here is the one southwest of Fujairah City (Al Ittihad, December 2022: about 20 km southwest of the city; Al Khaleej, 2013: about 15 km), reached from the city along Sheikh Khalifa Street and then a winding mountain road. The operator's pin is at 25.1108, 56.2236. MissionsOffroad gives a different start, 25.112677, 56.211266, near the petroglyph rock; confirm which one the signs lead to when you arrive.

The mountain is Jebel Riham (spelt Raham by some sources). Al Ittihad reports that Fujairah Adventures Centre renamed it and built dedicated mountain trails to its summit. Underfoot, ECC Adventures describes a steady ascent and descent with loose rocks, steep grades from the start, exposure to heights and full sun. It tells people with vertigo or a fear of heights not to join.

Landmarks named by the operator are archaeological sites along the way and the 'Jameel' Rock. ECC lists petroglyphs and views over mainland Fujairah, the sea, and the villages of Al Hayl and Saham. Do not touch or climb on rock art.

Official length is 7.71 km and official time 2 to 3 hours; about 450 to 470 m of climbing is reported by third parties. ECC describes a loop, and the operator does not give the turn-around or finish point, so follow the operator's map and do not assume you can cut the route short.

Waymarking: the operator says each of its trails is marked with a difficulty rating, and it publishes this trail in its Fujairah Trails app (links on its website). No source describes the markers on this trail, so download the route before you go and do not rely on finding signs.
bestMonths: December to March is the best period according to ECC Adventures, a guide company. The official hiking season opened on 25 September 2026 and its end date was not found; April and October to November are workable if you start early.
startAdvice: Start early. ECC Adventures meets its guests at 7:00 am and starts walking at 7:45 am; it says other months than December to March are hotter and need more water. No official start time is given.
shade: Little, according to ECC Adventures, which lists sun exposure as a challenge of this route. The operator gives no shade information.
water: The operator says the route passes water springs near the start, but not whether they flow or whether the water is drinkable, so carry all you need. ECC Adventures tells its guests to carry 1 to 2 litres from December to March and 2 to 3 litres in other months.
signal: unknown. No source opened gives mobile coverage for this trail.
fees: No fee for walkers was found on the Fujairah Adventures Centre website, last checked October 2026. Its permit services are for companies, event organisers and guides.
permits: No walker permit was found on the Fujairah Adventures Centre website, last checked October 2026. Its permit services are for companies, event organisers and guides. Its FAQ says: 'Hiking is allowed only during the official adventure season, announced annually on Fujairah Adventure social media platforms.' No group-size rule for hikers was found.
hours: No opening hours were found for this trail, last checked October 2026.
closure: None found for this trail, last checked October 2026. Khaleej Times and Zawya (1 October 2026) report that Fujairah reopened all its officially approved trails on 25 September 2026; neither names Al Riham, but the trail is on the operator's current list, updated August 2026. Al Khaleej (2013) reports that when Wadi Saham fills with water the road to the village can be cut off.
safety: The operator's FAQ says hiking is allowed only during the official adventure season, announced each year on Fujairah Adventures' social media. Check its channels before you go.

Al Riham is graded Hard by the operator. ECC Adventures describes steep grades from the start, loose rocks and exposure to heights, and advises against it for people with vertigo or a fear of heights.
Stay on the marked trail, tell someone your route and expected return time, and check the weather first.
Wadi Saham fills with water after rain and the road to the village can be cut off (Al Khaleej). Do not go in or near the wadi if rain has fallen or is forecast.
The route has little shade and full sun, so start early and carry more water than you expect to need.
Ancient petroglyphs and archaeological sites lie along the route. Do not touch or move them, and take your rubbish with you.
Pets are not allowed on most Fujairah Adventures trails; the operator names only Tayyibah and Seven Summits as pet-friendly.
carry: Fully charged phone with the route downloaded for offline use
emergency: Police 999, ambulance 998, fire and civil defence 997 (Ajman government emergency numbers page, opened October 2026; these are the UAE-wide numbers).
intro: Al Riham Trail climbs Jebel Riham from Wadi Saham, southwest of Fujairah City, and is the one route Fujairah Adventures Centre grades Hard. The operator lists 7.71 km and 2 to 3 hours, and third parties report about 450 m of climbing.

_doubts: Climb 450 m is third-party (MissionsOffroad 450 m; ECC Adventures 470 m). The operator gives no ascent, and its Wikiloc and AllTrails records could not be opened (Cloudflare 403 or robots block), so the exact figure for the operator's route is unconfirmed.

Shape 'loop' comes only from ECC Adventures' guided route. The operator does not say loop, return or one way, or whether 7.71 km is the whole route. MissionsOffroad and ECC give about 7 km, so the whole route is likely, but that is my inference.

Two start points: the operator's Google Maps pin (25.1108212, 56.2236185) and MissionsOffroad's Jebel Raham start (25.112677, 56.211266, about 1.3 km west, beside the petroglyph rock). ECC meets guests at the ADNOC station at the Fujairah entrance, not at the trailhead. Not reconciled; the page should link the operator's map and say a person must confirm the start on site.

Parking and vehicle: no source describes the car park or the road surface to the trailhead. Al Khaleej (2013) describes a winding mountain road to Wadi Saham village from Sheikh Khalifa Street, and MissionsOffroad says a 4x4 is needed for the wadi camping area (25.0889, 56.1973), not for the trail start. Both fields left null.

Which Wadi Saham: resolved as the one southwest of Fujairah City (Wikipedia coordinates 25.1128, 56.2089; Al Ittihad about 20 km southwest of the city; Al Khaleej about 15 km southwest; the operator's Al Riham pin; MissionsOffroad and ECC all agree). The operator's destination text 'Wadi Saham in Dibba' refers to a different place and does not apply. The 15 km and 20 km distances disagree; I give a range.

Grade disagreement: operator 'Hard' versus ECC Adventures 'Intermediate (6/10)'. The operator's grade is used. Time disagreement: operator 2 to 3 hours versus ECC 2.5 to 3.5 hours guided. Operator figures used as the headline.

Waymarking: the operator's FAQ says each trail is marked with difficulty ratings and Al Ittihad says it built trails to the summit, but no source describes markers on this trail. The December 2024 signage claims (The National) were for four other new trails.

Season: the 2026 to 2027 season opened 25 September 2026 (Khaleej Times, Zawya, 1 October 2026). No end date found. The operator's season announcements are on social media, which could not be read. No group-size or walker-permit rule was found; its permit pages are for companies, events and guides. Emarat Al Youm (11 October 2025) announced a 15th trail without naming it, so I could not tell if it is Riham.
months values are editorial: December to March best from ECC Adventures, the rest from the season opening date and UAE heat. No official month-by-month rating exists.

Fees, hours: none found for walkers (operator site, last checked October 2026). Mobile signal, wildlife and scrambling are unknown. The flood warning is general advice backed by Al Khaleej's note about the road.
Drive time from Dubai and Abu Dhabi: no source for this trail, so null.
Emergency numbers 999, 998 and 997 come from the Ajman government page only; a UAE federal page could not be opened (u.ae returned 404).

Tried and not obtained: Wikiloc (four Al Riham or Jebel Raham records, 403), AllTrails (robots), YouTube video (HTTP 429), Komoot, Outdooractive and Gaia (searches returned only Oman or unrelated pages), Strava and Relive (no results), UAE Trekkers (no Riham page found), WAM (no result), Al Bayan (no result), the operator's social posts (not readable), the operator feed (no elevation, gpx or track fields on the record). Sources not used: travelandtourworld.com (figures disagree with the operator).
Photos: the only Commons files found for Wadi Saham show petroglyph rocks, not the trail; they are in the same wadi as the MissionsOffroad start point. No trail photos found.

Second choice if Al Riham is dropped: Dhanha (Rainbow) Trail, Dibba, graded Extreme by the operator, 6.0 km, 120 to 180 minutes, pin 25.578877, 56.186329. Its grade is above Difficult and I did not research it further.
